comments.body: Hi! Gentle ping in case this slipped through — it still merges cleanly with main. Happy to adjust anything if you'd prefer a different approach. Thanks for maintaining this!

Thanks for the fix, @pcbeingused333! Leaving modified clicks to the browser is the right call. It's the same convention web routers follow.

I merged the newest `main` and pushed a small follow-up (6f9f4b80):

- **Tests:** since #1225, `LinkRenderer` uses `useContext`, so calling it as a plain function threw on `main`. I replaced the tests with `src/web/__tests__/linkClick.test.tsx`, which renders `EnrichedMarkdownText` and dispatches real `MouseEvent`s:
  - a plain click calls `onLinkPress` and is prevented;
  - Cmd/Ctrl/Shift-clicks on `https`, relative (`docs/page`, `../page`) and `tel:` links are left to the browser;
  - a Cmd-click on a custom scheme (`user://`) still goes to `onLinkPress`.
- **Which URLs the browser gets:** a modified click now goes to the browser for any URL without a scheme (relative paths, `#`, `?`) and for `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `tel` and `sms` links. Leading whitespace is trimmed first. Custom schemes keep going to `onLinkPress`, so mentions and similar links still work.
- **Dead check:** removed `event.button !== 0`. A middle-click fires `auxclick`, not `click`, so that branch could never run.
- **Docs:** one line in the web support guide describing the modified-click behaviour.

Verified: the full jest suite (2099 tests), `typecheck` and `eslint` pass. Thanks again for the contribution!

No actionable comments were generated in the recent review.

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title "fix(web): leave modified clicks on browser-openable links to the browser" matches the main change. The summaries show that modified clicks (Meta, Ctrl, Shift, Alt) on relative, http, https, mailto, tel, and sms links are left to the browser in LinkRenderer, with matching tests and a docs line. The title is specific, uses a conventional prefix, and does not describe anything absent from the changeset.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#1084`] requires that, with onLinkPress set, modified clicks on browser-openable links are left to the browser, plain clicks still call onLinkPress and are prevented, and custom-scheme links still reach onLinkPress. At head, InlineRenderers.tsx adds isBrowserOpenable(url), which returns true for relative URLs and for http, https, mailto, tel, and sms after trimming. LinkRenderer's handleClick returns early, without preventDefault, when a meta, ctrl, shift, or alt key is held and the URL is browser-openable. Other clicks fall through to the existing onLinkPress path. Custom schemes such as user:// are not browser-openable, so they still reach onLinkPress with modifiers held. The follow-up objective removes the event.button !== 0 check because middle-click fires auxclick, not click. The head code has no button check, which matches that objective. The test file linkClick.test.tsx renders EnrichedMarkdownText and dispatches real MouseEvents. It covers plain clicks, modified clicks on https, relative, and tel links, and a modified click on user://. Both the code and the tests support the requirement. The web example was not run in a browser, so runtime behavior in a real browser is not verified.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The whole-PR diff against the merge base touches three files. InlineRenderers.tsx holds the scheme classifier and the modified-click branch that implement `#1084`. linkClick.test.tsx tests that branch. web-support.md adds one line describing the modified-click behavior, which documents the change. No unrelated code, API, or declaration changes were found. The current PR description still mentions a non-primary-button check and a test file name that differ from head. These are description inaccuracies, not out-of-scope code.
